problem: Eliminate the crash window between mission mutation commit and durable request-result journal completion.

candidates.name: unified-atomic-snapshot
candidates.notes: Mission state and request outcome share one lock and one atomic rename. Straightforward deterministic crash testing. Full-file rewrite remains LAB-scale.

candidates.name: two-store-reconciliation
candidates.notes: Smaller initial refactor, but ambiguous in-progress outcomes require action-specific inference and more recovery branches.

candidates.name: sqlite-transaction
candidates.notes: Strongest local transactional semantics and scale, but adds a new dependency/storage migration before the existing JSON queue is stabilized.

candidates.name: external-transactional-coordinator
candidates.notes: Best future multi-Qube direction, but premature before qrexec deployment, secret lifecycle, and local failure semantics are fully validated.

why: It closes the known LAB crash-consistency gap with one atomic persistence boundary, minimal new dependencies, low protocol churn, and strong deterministic QA. SQLite/external coordination remain stronger future migration targets once multi-Qube throughput and deployment requirements justify them.
failuresAndLessons: Separate atomic files are not a transaction: either file may commit before coordinator death.
Reconciliation pushes ambiguity into action-specific recovery logic and increases regression surface.
Atomic rename protects the visible snapshot, but full-file JSON rewrite is not the final high-throughput distributed design.
The unified store must be integrated into DurableMissionQueue and JournaledCoordinator before this gate is considered fully closed.
